 This Mfa, Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment

Heard Sri.Mallikarjun Doddabasavarajappa Ryakha, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.Pradeep B., learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
2.
This is the claimant's appeal.
Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru in M.V.C No.596/2019 dated 16.11.2021.
3. As against the claim for Rs.20,00,000/-, the Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.6,20,715/- as compensation and aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed.

Sri.Mallikarjun Doddabasavarajappa Ryakha, learned counsel for the appellant, arguing the matter, submits that the appellant sustained four grievous injuries due to the accident and became permanently disabled.
However, without at least assessing the proper monthly income of the appellant, the Tribunal awarded a very meagre sum as compensation.
Learned counsel also states that the appellant, as a skilled mason and painter, was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

Learned counsel also states that the accident occurred in the year 2019 and for the relevant period, the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking notional income as Rs.14,000/- per month and the said figure ought to have been considered by the Tribunal at least.
Learned counsel also states that though PW-2 deposed before the Court that disability in respect of whole body is 22%, the Tribunal took the same as 15%, which is unjustifiable.
Learned counsel further contends that the amount granted as compensation under all other heads are also on lower side.
Therefore, learned counsel, seeks for enhancement of compensation.

The NC: 2024:KHC:32202 compensation that is granted by the Tribunal under each head is as under:-

2  Heads Amount Pain and sufferings Rs. 65,000/-
Loss of amenities Rs. 60,000/-
Nursing, attendants, extra Rs. 25,000/-
nourishment and conveyance Loss of earning during Rs. 36,000/-
treatment

Loss of future income Rs. 2,43,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs. 1,91,715/-
 Total Rs. 6,20,715/-
5.

The submission that is made by Sri.Pradeep B., learned counsel for respondent No.2 is that the appellant has not produced any proof with regard to his occupation and earnings by the date of the accident.
Further, there is no proof to show that he is disabled and is not attending any work.
Learned counsel also contends that the Tribunal taking the totality of evidence into consideration awarded just sum as compensation, which requires no interference.
6. As rightly contended, no substantive proof is produced with regard to the actual occupation and earnings of the appellant by the date of accident.

NC: 2024:KHC:32202 However, this Court does not find any reason to discard the submission made by the learned counsel for the appellant that the amount as assessed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority as notional income ought to have been taken into consideration by the Tribunal.

This Court considers it necessary to take the notional income of the appellant as Rs.14,000/- per month.
7. By the contents of Ex.P5-wound certificate, it is clear that the appellant sustained Subtrochateric fracture of left hip, communited Right Distal Radius Fracture, Communited Left Distal Radius Fracture and Grade-II Compound Communited Celcarem Fracture, which are grievous in nature.
There is no dispute of the fact that the appellant was aged about 40 years by the date of the accident.

On perusing of the relevant material that is brought on record including evidence of PW-2, this Court is of the view that the disability as assessed by the Tribunal in respect of whole body needs no interference.

Also, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NC:
2024:KHC:32202 National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the actual earnings are required to be added towards future prospects.

sentences.text: Further, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is '15' as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298.

sentences.text:
On applying the aforementioned parameters, the loss of earnings due to permanent disability will be as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Notional monthly income 14,000-00 Annual income 1,68,000-00 (14,000 x 12)
Add 40% towards future 2,35,200-00

3 prospects
Appropriate multiplier '15' 35,28,000-00 15% being permanent 5,29,200-00 physical disability

8. Taking into consideration the fact that the appellant sustained four grievous injuries, and also underwent surgery, this Court is of the view that the appellant would not have attended his normal pursuits at NC: 2024:KHC:32202 least for a period of three months.
Therefore, loss of earnings during the laid up period comes to Rs.42,000/- (14,000 x 3).
This Court is of the view that the appellant is entitled to Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering.

Thus, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to is as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 80,000-00 Loss of amenities in life 60,000-00

Nursing, attendant, extra 25,000-00 nourishment and conveyance charges Loss of earning during laid- 42,000-00 up period Loss of future earnings due 5,29,200-00 to permanent physical disability Medical expenses 1,91,715-00
Thus, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to is Rs.9,27,915/-.

Therefore, the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru through order NC: 2024:KHC:32202 in M.V.C No.596/2019 dated 16.11.2021 is enhanced from Rs.6,20,715/- to Rs.9,27,915/-.
iii. The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv. The 2nd respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
v. On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
